newsitem.title: MEXICO: Volcano belches ash, smoke close to Mexico City.
newsitem.headline: Volcano belches ash, smoke close to Mexico City.

text.p: A volcano close to Mexico's capital suddenly belched a thick column of ash and smoke two miles (three km) into the sky early Monday but initial reports said residents were in no immediate danger.

The Popocatepetl volcano, part of a mountain chain bordering the eastern side of the Valley of Mexico in which the capital lies, started belching at around 9.05 a.m. (1505 GMT), the Televisa television network reported.

Televisa showed live pictures of billowing clouds of ash emerging from the crater of the volcano. It quoted local officials as saying that most of the ash was likely to be deposited over rural areas of the states of Morelos and Puebla, to the south and east of Mexico City.
The explosion that preceded Monday's belching was felt in small towns and villages near the volcano but civil defence officials said they saw no need for evacuations.

Guillermo Melgarejo, an official of the Puebla state civil protection system, told the official news agency Notimex that the explosion was the "natural product of the volcano's activity" and Popocatepetl remained geologically stable.
The 17,760-foot (5,465-metre)-high Popocatepetl has had frequent minor belches of smoke and ash in recent years but has not erupted lava or fire for hundreds of years.
